To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
A generic HPLC method was successfully developed and transferred to reduce the analysis times for the quantification of 2 WHO-recommended anti-malarial tablets.
a generic liquid chromatography method was successfully developed, transferred and validated for the purpose of analyzing two WHO recommended antimalarial tablets.

A new generic liquid chromatographic (LC) method was developed and optimized using Design of Experiments and Data Analysis strategy for the purpose of simultaneous determination of 8 antimalariar active ingredients in tablets.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of generic methods for the analysis of antimalarial active pharmaceutical ingredients (API) and their application for the analysis of tablets.
the development, transfer and validation of a generic high-performance liquid chromatographic method for analyzing two WHO recommended antimalarial tablets.
the development, transfer and validation of generic HPLC methods for analyzing two WHO recommended antimalarial tablets.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a generic HPLC method was developed for the screening of eight antimalarial drugs and successfully applied to the quantification of AM-LF and AS/AQ in antimalarial tablets marketed in Africa.
the developed methods were robust and reliable for the quantification of the two WHO-recommended antimalarial medicines in tablets.
the developed and validated method is suitable for routine use in pharmaceutical quality control laboratories.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the proposed methods could be used as screening and quality control tools for antimalarial fixed-dose combination tablets.
the developed method could be considered as an efficient tool to control the quality of antimalarial drugs in the market.
the proposed methods were developed to meet the analytical needs of antimalarial medicines in Africa.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the generic HPLC method is a promising tool to be used for screening of antimalarial medicines.
the developed method could be used for quality control of the two antimalarial fixed-dose combination tablets, and it could also be applied to the other antimalarial fixed dose combination tablets.
a generic method was successfully developed for the purpose to analyze the content of two antimalarial tablets in the market, which is a useful tool to fight the poor quality medicines.
